claims.text: What the strip looks like A paced tachycardia whose maximum rate is limited by the pacemaker programming.
claims.quote: Results in a paced tachycardia with the maximum rate limited by the pacemaker programming

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Rate: paced tachycardia, capped at the programmed maximum rate
claims.quote: Results in a paced tachycardia with the maximum rate limited by the pacemaker programming

claims.text: P waves: retrograde P waves, which may be buried in the QRS complexes or T waves
claims.quote: Pacemaker-mediated tachycardia (with retrograde P waves buried in the QRS complexes /T waves).

claims.text: Differential for a rapid ventricular-paced rhythm with no preceding atrial activity: pacemaker-mediated tachycardia, sensor-induced tachycardia, or potentially normal with an appropriate physiological stimulus (e.g., exercise)
claims.quote: There is a rapid ventricular-paced rhythm (120 bpm) with no evidence of preceding atrial activity (except for the first complex). The differential diagnosis of this rhythm would include: Pacemaker-mediated tachycardia (with retrograde P waves buried in the QRS complexes /T waves). Sensor-induced tachycardia. Could potentially be normal in the presence of an appropriate physiological stimulus (e.g. exercise).

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: a re-entry tachycardia — the pacemaker forms the antegrade pathway and retrograde conduction runs through the AV node
claims.quote: PMT is a re-entry tachycardia in which the pacemaker forms the antegrade pathway with retrograde conduction occurring via the AV node

claims.text: Retrograde P waves are sensed as native atrial activity and trigger ventricular pacing; each paced beat conducts back again, forming a continuous cycle
claims.quote: Caused by retrograde p waves being sensed as native atrial activity with subsequent ventricular pacing The paced ventricular complex results in further retrograde conduction with retrograde p wave generation thus forming a continuous cycle
Also known as endless-loop tachycardia or pacemaker circus movement tachycardia.

claims.text: Symptoms May cause rate-related ischemia when ischemic heart disease is present
claims.quote: May result in rate related ischaemia in the presences of IHD

claims.text: Treatment Terminate it by slowing AV conduction (e.g., adenosine) or by activating magnet mode
claims.quote: Can be terminated by slowing AV conduction e.g. adenosine or activation of magnet mode

claims.text: Newer pacemakers have programmed algorithms designed to terminate PMT
claims.quote: Newer pacemakers contain programmed algorithms designed to terminate PMT

notes.issue: the rhythm "this rhythm" refers to was outside the quote, and the claim dropped "could potentially"
notes.resolution: quote now starts at "There is a rapid ventricular-paced rhythm (120 bpm) with no evidence of preceding atrial activity…"; claim scoped to that rhythm and says "potentially normal"; re-checked pass
